cases.situation: Had a final-round interview yesterday for a product designer role at Loop Health with the head of design, Marcus. He talked a lot about their accessibility audit. I fumbled a question about design systems.
cases.reply:
Hi Marcus,
Thank you for the conversation yesterday. Your point about the accessibility audit changing how the team prioritises the backlog stuck with me; it's the kind of work I'd want to be part of. One thing I'd add to my answer on design systems: at Fenwick I set up the shared component library in Figma that cut our handoff time roughly in half, which I didn't explain well in the moment. I'm very interested in the role and happy to send anything else that helps.
Best,
Alina
cases.note: Within 24 hours, one specific thing he said, one clarification, one line of interest. Not a second cover letter.

cases.situation: 今天下午和合作方开了项目启动会，定了几件事：先做华东区试点，对方的孙经理负责提供门店数据，我负责出排期。想发个会后纪要。
cases.reply:
各位好，感谢今天的时间，简单整理一下会议结论，确保大家理解一致：
- 先做华东区试点，覆盖上海和杭州共12家门店。
- 孙经理：10月9日前提供门店销售数据。
- 我：10月10日前发出完整排期。
- 待定：试点期间是否需要法务审核活动规则，由赵律师10月8日前确认。
如有记错的地方请直接指出。
陈静
cases.note: 会后纪要当天发，每一项都有负责人和日期，写下你希望成为事实的版本。

cases.situation: Interviewed for an account manager job at a logistics company 3 weeks ago, the recruiter Hannah said I'd hear back by last Friday. Nothing. I already sent one check-in 10 days ago.
cases.reply: Hi Hannah, I'll take the quiet as the timing not working out on your side. Thanks again for a well-run process, and I'd be glad to hear from you if a similar role opens up at Crestline.
cases.note: One check-in was already sent, so this is the short closing note. It leaves a good last impression without chasing.

cases.situation: Got a rejection email this morning from Harbor Food Bank for the program manager role, after the final round. The director, Grace, was lovely and I'd genuinely want to work there someday.
cases.reply:
Hi Grace,
Thank you for letting me know, and for a process that was genuinely well run. Our conversation about moving the pantry network to appointment-based pickups has stayed with me. If it's possible, I'd value one line on what tipped the decision. Either way, I'd be glad to hear from you if a similar role opens up.
Best,
Marcus
cases.note: After a no: reply once, ask for one line of feedback, then stop. The specific callback is what gets you remembered for the next opening.

cases.situation: 今天约了行业前辈刘老师喝咖啡，聊了一个小时。她建议我找一个产品从头到尾拆一遍，推荐了《用户体验要素》，还说可以把我介绍给她在字节的前同事陈磊。想发微信谢谢她。
cases.reply: 刘老师，谢谢您今天抽出一个小时跟我聊。您说的“找一个产品从头到尾拆一遍”对我特别有用，我这周就按《用户体验要素》把飞书文档拆一遍，周日前整理好发您看看。您提到可以介绍陈磊，我先写一段简短的自我介绍发您，您觉得合适再转给他就好。
cases.note: Networking follow-up: quote her own advice back, show you're acting on it with a date, and make the introduction easy for her to pass on.

cases.situation: At a trade show yesterday I talked for 10 minutes at our booth with Priyanka, head of procurement at Aster Hotels. We sell commercial laundry equipment. She said they're replacing machines at 3 properties next spring and asked about energy use. I have her card.
cases.reply:
Subject: Energy figures for the Aster laundry refit

Hi Priyanka, thanks for stopping by our stand at HospitalityX yesterday. You asked about energy use: our HX-40 washers use about 30 percent less power per load than the 2018 models most hotels are replacing, and the one-page spec with the figures is attached. If it would help your spring planning, I can send an estimate for all three properties by Friday 16 October. Would that be useful?
cases.note: Answer the one question she actually asked, then offer a small next step, not a demo call.

cases.situation: After Monday's kickoff with our design agency I sent a recap saying they'd deliver wireframes by Friday Oct 9. Their lead, Tom, replied-all: 'That's not what we agreed, we said the 9th for the homepage only and the other pages the week after.' Thinking back, he's probably right.
cases.reply: Thanks for the correction, Tom. I've updated the notes: homepage wireframes by Friday Oct 9, the remaining pages by Friday Oct 16. Everything else in the recap stands. Shout if anything else is off.
cases.note: When a recap gets pushback, correct it, thank them and move on. Arguing about who said what in a reply-all costs more than the date.

cases.situation: Had my 1:1 with my manager Dana today about getting promoted to senior engineer. She said if I lead the billing migration and mentor our new hire Theo, she'll put me forward in the March cycle. I want it in writing without sounding like I'm lawyering her.
cases.reply:
Hi Dana,
Thanks for the time today, it was really useful to hear exactly what the path to senior looks like. Quick recap so we're aligned:
- I'll lead the billing migration, with cutover planned for 15 January.
- I'll mentor Theo through his first quarter, and we'll review how that's going at the end of December.
- If both land, you'll put me forward in the March promotion cycle.
Shout if I've got anything wrong. I'll bring a progress update to our 1:1 on Tuesday 3 November.
Maya
cases.note: A career conversation is a meeting too: the recap with owners and dates is what turns 'if you do this' into something both of you remember the same way.

cases.situation: I'm an internal candidate for team lead on our support team. Interviewed yesterday with the director, Renata. She asked how I'd lead people who were my peers until last week, and I think my answer was too vague. Want to send her a thank-you on Slack.
cases.reply: Hi Renata, thanks for the interview yesterday, and for being so direct about what the first 90 days would look like. Your question about leading people who've been my peers is the one I've kept thinking about, so here's the clearer answer: I'd hold a one-to-one with each of the six of us in my first two weeks, agree how we'll handle disagreements, and keep taking a share of the escalation queue so I stay close to the work. I'd really like this role, and I'm happy to talk it through further before you decide.
cases.note: Internal follow-up: keep it short and in the channel you normally use, and spend it fixing the one weak answer rather than repeating the pitch.
